A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PiNDA research, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. V1 has no separate appendix; v2 includes complete Appendices A–C. Relocated derivations and experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments on six datasets, noise visualizations, convergence curves, and computational-cost measurements in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional dataset evaluations, baseline comparisons, generator ablations, and resource analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: V2 introduces U-Net as an alternative noise-generator architecture in Section 4.3.4 and Table 6, extending v1's DNN/ResNet implementations. The PiNDA objective, reparameterization, augmentation selection, and joint training remain unchanged. Algorithm 1's sampling-notation correction agrees with the distribution already specified in v1's prose.

E1.justification: V2 retains the six original datasets and adds Epsilon, MSLR-WEB30K, Reuters-21578, and ImageNet. These extend coverage to additional binary-classification data, query–URL relevance data, a 46-class text dataset, and large-scale image classification. Reuters-21578 is evaluated separately from the retained four-class Reuters subset.

E2.justification: V2 adds transformer-based DINO to the ImageNet comparison in Table 5 and SAM-derived background-noise augmentation to comparisons on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, and ImageNet in Tables 7–8. The original comparator suite is retained. These additions substantially broaden the comparison beyond the earlier contrastive models and noise augmentations.

E3.justification: V2 adds ImageNet evaluation at 96×96 resolution within 100 training epochs, an STL-10 batch-size sweep from 256 to 4096 using 32×32 images and 100 epochs, and comparisons of PiNDA at batch 256 against baseline batch 300 under similar memory use. Table 3 changes the reported ResNet18 SimCLR batch size from 64 to 256 while retaining existing scores. Table 1 also revises CIFAR sizes from 70,000 to 60,000 and STL-10 from 13,000 to 113,000; these revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's noise-distribution and mean ablations, visualizations, convergence plots, and cost measurements, v2 adds generator accuracy-versus-cost comparisons, a larger batch-size sensitivity study, SAM background-augmentation comparisons, non-vision resource measurements, and similar-memory controls (Table 6, Figure 5, and Appendix C). The original convergence and visualization analyses are retained, mostly through relocation.

E5.justification: Tables 2–4 retain five-run averages and ± reporting, and the new SAM comparison in Table 7 follows that practice. However, new ImageNet results in Tables 5 and 8, generator results in Table 6, and the batch-size chart report point estimates without corresponding run counts or uncertainty. This changes reporting practice without establishing a reduction in actual repetitions.

E6.justification: The original HAR/Reuters and Fashion-MNIST/STL-10 accuracy entries are unchanged, and Table 3 adds three learned-mean ablation rows. Substantial new results cover the added datasets, comparators, and controls: for example, v2 Table 5 reports ImageNet SR accuracy of 64.18 for SimCLR and 66.86 with PiNDA. Generator results also expose failures, including 58.28 SR for U-Net with the ResNet18 ImageNet backbone in Table 6. Resource measurements are revised: the STL-10 baseline changes from 85 seconds and 15.68G in v1 Table 5 to 21 seconds and 48.20G in v2 Table 9, without enough matched-setting information to infer an efficiency gain.

T1.justification: The auxiliary Gaussian definition, task entropy, point-estimation argument, and PiNDA derivation retain their mathematical substance. V1's Equation (17) derivation is reproduced in v2 Appendix A to support Equation (13). Other changes consolidate, renumber, or restate existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contribution claims about task entropy, augmentation as point-estimated noise, and learning transferable augmentations remain intact. V2's conclusion adds a practical claim that PiNDA improves accuracy under similar computational expenses, supported specifically by the similar-memory comparison in Table 11. Removing the introductory experimental-contribution bullet does not remove its claim elsewhere.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of SAM's preprocessing cost, generator architecture tradeoffs, and the benefits of PiNDA versus increasing batch size (Appendices C.2, C.4, and C.5.1). It recommends ResNet18 on cost–performance grounds, discusses U-Net training difficulty, and proposes parameter sharing as future work. Earlier interpretations concerning background suppression, learnable means, and convergence are preserved.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code repository address where v1 promised release after publication, documents image resolutions, and explains offline SAM preprocessing. Most existing architecture, optimizer, projection-head, and evaluation details are retained in Appendix B. Conversely, v2 removes v1's specific GPU model and memory-capacity disclosures. The repository's availability is asserted by the PDF and was not independently checked.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting DINO, SAM, U-Net, the additional datasets, and several newer related works. It removes citations and discussion concerning LightGCL, supervised contrastive learning, contrastive clustering, and hypergraph augmentation. The central positioning relative to positive-incentive noise and existing augmentation approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the document: it consolidates the optimization-goal subsection, moves derivation details into Appendix A, redistributes experimental settings into Appendix B, and organizes much of the analysis into Appendix C. The main experimental narrative gains dedicated generator and batch-size sections. Much individual prose is retained, but the reading structure changes extensively.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different conference layout, reduces Figures 1 and 4 to single-column displays, and relocates full-width visualizations to the appendix. It adds six tables and a batch-size bar chart, expands existing tables, and redraws the convergence plots with changed colors and axes. V1 Figures 5–7 correspond to v2 Figures 6–8, so these are retained displays rather than new analyses.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly lacked ImageNet evaluation and relied on two small non-vision datasets. V2 substantially strengthens evidence for general applicability through broader, larger-scale evaluations. SAM comparisons, generator ablations, and similar-memory controls also test practical alternatives and resource tradeoffs that v1 left unresolved. These gains outweigh the reporting weaknesses, although point-only ImageNet estimates, unexplained batch-size and cost revisions, and removed hardware details still limit confidence and reproducibility.
